title: Protocol: Black Knight
premise: A mobile-first top-down action encounter where a lone containment operative roams a dark techno-urban district, triggers a breach, and must defeat the summoned Black Knight in a single high-pressure boss duel.
interaction_model: Real-time touch controls with a virtual joystick for movement and large on-screen action buttons for attack, breach summon, and parry timing.
objective: Summon the Black Knight, survive its melee and projectile patterns, parry at the correct moment to create stun windows, and reduce its health to zero before the player's HP is depleted.
progression: Short menu onboarding leads into a roaming setup phase, then a summoning transition, followed by a single boss fight that ends in either victory or defeat before resetting for another run.
theme: Sci-fi containment ritual blended with dark knight boss combat in a neon, void-tinted city arena.
mood: Tense, stylish, reactive, and arcade-like with dramatic audiovisual feedback.
likely_audience: casual players who enjoy readable timing mechanics
confidence_notes: High confidence that the intended core is a one-boss top-down action duel.
High confidence that parry timing is the signature mechanic and the main source of mastery.
Moderate confidence that the roam phase is mostly atmospheric setup rather than a deep exploratory mode.
Low confidence on any narrative depth beyond the containment framing shown in UI text.
recreation_prompt: Create a polished mobile-first top-down action boss duel called "Protocol: Black Knight" set in a dark neon techno-city containment zone. The game should open with a stylish title screen and brief instructions, then place the player in a sparse scrolling district viewed from above, with a glowing blue cyber-operative controlled by a left-side virtual joystick and right-side action buttons. The early phase is a short roaming setup space with scattered building obstacles, ambient NPC civilians, a player HP display, and moody roaming background music. A prominent "Breach" button should let the player deliberately summon the Black Knight, triggering a dark portal or fountain effect, screen shake, stronger combat music, removal of civilians, and the appearance of a boss health bar. The core gameplay loop is a single boss encounter focused on spacing, timing, and readable attack patterns: the boss chases the player, performs a close-range slash with a visible windup when near, and throws a spinning projectile when farther away. The player can make short-range melee strikes with an attack button and can use a parry button with a cooldown to block an incoming slash or projectile during a tight timing window; a successful parry should negate damage, create bright defensive feedback, and stun the boss long enough for safe punishment attacks. Missing the timing should cause heavy player damage, knockback, hit effects, and an eventual game-over state if HP reaches zero. Present the whole experience with strong arcade juice such as particles, floating damage numbers, screen shake, glowing UI, and end screens for defeat and victory, keeping the progression to a single contained run that can be immediately retried.
